page_title: ARM’s Neoverse N2: Cortex A710 for Servers

sources.entry: ARM's Neoverse N2: Cortex A710 for Servers - Measures structure sizes, cache latencies and mesh behaviour of N2 on Yitian, the core Cobalt 100 carries.

summary.title: ARM's Neoverse N2: Cortex A710 for Servers
summary.one_liner: Neoverse N2 is a server-oriented version of the Cortex A710 core, and this article measures its structures, caches and mesh behaviour on Alibaba's Yitian 710, comparing it with AMD Zen 4 and Intel Sapphire Rapids.
keywords: how do arm server cores compare to x86
why is server cpu l3 latency high
takeaways: Neoverse N2 is a 5-wide out-of-order core closely matching the Cortex A710, with 64 KB L1 caches, 1 MB L2 and 48-bit physical addressing.
N2 has a smaller ROB (160 entries) and TLBs than Zen 4, but a competitive scheduler layout and two branches per cycle.
Mesh-based L3 on Yitian 710 has high latency (about 35 ns at 16 MB) and DRAM latency of 141 ns, so high L2 hitrates matter.
Yitian 710 DRAM bandwidth (about 112 GB/s) beats Ice Lake in this test, while AMD's Zen 3 L3 bandwidth is far higher.
N2 is an upgrade over N1, but the author expects it to trail x86 cores on vector code and wished for more aggressive changes.
summary.summary: The article is a microarchitecture analysis of ARM's Neoverse N2 (Cortex A710 derivative), measured on an octa-core Alibaba Yitian 710 cloud instance. The author covers the block diagram, branch prediction, out-of-order execution, FP/vector units, TLBs, physical address size, cache setup, L3 and DRAM latency and bandwidth, instruction-side bandwidth and core-to-core latency. Comparisons are made against AMD Zen 4, Zen 3 (Epyc 7763), Intel Sapphire Rapids and Ice Lake, and Ampere Altra. Where ARM published figures the author uses them, and otherwise the numbers come from microbenchmarks on the cloud instance.
